props.title: Believe Anything
lines: Stories are how we stitch incomplete facts into a feeling of control.
The more you want the world to be predictable, the more fiction you will accept.

rows.v: 85% of active mutual funds underperformed their benchmarks in the span the book cites.
A Fed forecast once gave 1.6% to 2.8% growth as its band — then missed by more than 2%.
A Pluto flyby forecast 99.99998% accurate. Money is not a spacecraft. We still want that feeling.
Kahneman: founders say at least 80% of the outcome depends on what they do inside the firm.
A 1% chance of getting rich without effort is easy to over-weight if you cannot calibrate small odds.

A 1.6% to 2.8% growth band, then a miss of more than 2%. Official stories drift too.
A flyby at 99.99998% accuracy. We crave that feeling in markets and invent it.
Founders tell Kahneman that at least 80% of the outcome is what they do inside the firm.

props.title: Keep the story thinner than the cash
items: Prefer rules that survive a wrong story: save, diversify, avoid ruin, stay for tails.
When a forecast feels perfectly tight, remember the Fed miss and the 85% of funds.
